title: Track installed guidance snippets and updates
description:
Design and implement a lightweight, reliable way for guidance-composer to determine:
- which guidance snippets are already installed
- whether any installed snippets need updating

Produce a proposal for principal approval before implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Proposal documents the data model, detection algorithm, update semantics, and failure behavior.
2. Implementation begins only after proposal approval.
3. Installed snippets can be identified without expensive scanning or network dependence.
4. Changed source snippets are reported as needing update.
5. Tests cover installed, current, outdated, missing, and corrupted metadata cases.
notes:
Initial proposal was rejected because verbose per-ID/hash metadata would bloat the managed region.

Principal feedback verbatim: "I do NOT like this approach, it is going to heavily bloat the managed region, what about a bitmask?"

Follow-up requirement: design the smallest reliable bitmask-based representation. Explain why a bare installed mask is or is not sufficient for freshness, define stable catalog indexing/version semantics, migration and corruption behavior, and quantify managed-region bytes. Proposal only; do not implement.

title: Calibrate model routing from historical work outcomes
description: After the routing-criteria review, design and implement a retrospective procedure that mines any available Codex, Claude Code, or Grok session using a configured model and effort. Jev involvement and a routing-journal link are not eligibility conditions for model-performance learning. Split sessions into work units and attribute each to the model and effort that did the work, including model switches. Resolve task references; inspect user feedback, artifacts, tests, errors, and abandonment; distinguish changed requirements and external failures from model errors. Classify each unit across a thorough multi-label domain taxonomy and score only domains with specific outcome evidence. Keep private assessment evidence locally; publish aggregate, non-identifying findings with sample size, uncertainty, shrinkage for sparse cells, and bounded outlier influence. Audit Jev labels. Evaluate routing decisions separately through exact worker-session links, and compare the router to a mechanical/agent baseline on comparable tasks. Revisit score dimensions, cost-quality value, benchmark scales, and preferences; replace score tables only when evidence supports it.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible retrospective pipeline processes all eligible local sessions, explains exclusions, segments mixed-model work, and reports evidenced domain-level quality with sample size and uncertainty; ambiguous outcomes remain unscored; routing-policy validation uses exact decision links separately; the user reviews calibration before automatic score updates.
notes:
Use docs/research/model-routing-value-proposal-2026-09-24.md as the starting design after criteria review. Retrospective unit is one delegated outcome with artifact/user evidence; Jev classifications alone cannot score visual quality. Add Score/Noul support and shadow-value evaluation before switching selectors.
2026-09-24 pilot: docs/research/model-routing-session-mining-2026-09-24.md defines 20 work domains and reports 17 historical Jev-assessed sessions across five model/effort settings. Jev marked 82 session-domain cells involved, but 70 quality cells unknown; no calibrated capability update. Before production, add task-level segmentation, artifact evidence, linked worker outcomes, subject-matter facets, and rubric false-positive checks.
2026-09-24 correction: any informative session with a configured model and effort can support model-domain performance analysis. Routing links are required only for evaluating the router policy. Full local matching census: 1,909 sessions; 1,821 projectable by the current bounded single-model parser. See docs/research/model-routing-labeling-and-history-audit-2026-09-24.md.

title: Review model-routing criteria and Jev value
description: Review docs/research/model-routing-criteria-audit-2026-09-24.md and docs/research/model-routing-retrospective-pilot-2026-09-24.md with the user. Decide which routing criteria remain useful, whether Jev adds outcome value beyond mechanical gates, and which benchmark dimensions or preferences to revise before outcome calibration.
acceptance_criteria: User-reviewed criteria decisions are recorded; unresolved questions are explicit; the retrospective-calibration epic can then begin.
notes: Proposal for review: docs/research/model-routing-value-proposal-2026-09-24.md. Live pilot found meaningful task/domain classification but no linked verified worker outcomes; current catalog lacks art-quality data. Keep this review open until the user accepts or revises the proposed division of labor and outage fallback.
